author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Professional football matches in the Netherlands will be abandoned when fireworks are used in the stands under a new safety agreement reported Friday. The policy was reached by the Dutch football federation KNVB, the Public Prosecution Service and Justice and Security Minister David van Weel.

The measure follows an incident during SC Cambuur’s league match against Feyenoord in Leeuwarden last month. Fireworks thrown by visiting supporters left several fans with burns, hearing damage and eye injuries, according to Reuters.

Stopping a match entirely is a stronger response than a temporary suspension. The agreement gives teams, officials and supporters a clear consequence when pyrotechnics are ignited, while authorities work to reduce injuries and disorder inside stadiums.

Implementation details, including how officials will handle identification, announcements and any appeals, were not set out in the initial report. The policy nevertheless changes the immediate calculus for clubs and fans: a single fireworks incident can now end the contest instead of merely delaying it. Dutch football authorities will be watched for how consistently the rule is applied across venues and competitions.
dek: The national federation, prosecutors and justice ministry agreed on the tougher response after fans were injured last month.
headline: Dutch football will abandon matches when fireworks are used
